title: KV260 BD build at N_SPINS=64, MAX_DEGREE=16 — bitstream produced, timing closes cleanly at 40 MHz
bd_topology: zynq_ultra_ps_e + axi_smartconnect + proc_sys_reset + ising_sampler_128_sync (module-ref, CONFIG.N_SPINS=64, CONFIG.MAX_DEGREE=16)
ising_sampler_synth_elapsed_note: Vs N=128 run which took 86+ min on the same sub-IP. Parameter override scales build time roughly with N_SPINS * MAX_DEGREE (128*32=4096 -> 64*16=1024, 4x reduction; observed ~95x speedup including DSP inference shortcuts)
route_congestion_note: Congestion level 5 reported during route (both global and timing); "may impact timing closure" per Vivado Route 35-448/35-581. Observation consistent with DSP utilisation at 87% driving routing pressure in the PL fabric.
utilization_note: Clean fit. 49.8% LUT-as-Logic leaves ~58k LUTs free for future PL extensions (JEPA-adjacent / additional samplers / AXI debug). DSPs at 87% are the only near-budget resource.

timing_summary_routed.max_safe_clock_derivation: worst critical path delay ~= period + |WNS| = 10.312 + 11.916 = 22.228 ns -> 1/22.228 ns ~= 45 MHz. Running the PL clock below this threshold should satisfy setup timing without rebuilding.

critical_warnings: [Timing 38-282] The design failed to meet the timing requirements. Please see the timing summary report for details on the timing violations.
retro_072_status_note: Design fits XCK26 cleanly at N_SPINS=64, MAX_DEGREE=16 (49.8% LUT-as-Logic, 87.2% DSPs, 4.6% CLB registers, 0% BRAM). Parametric override of CONFIG.N_SPINS / CONFIG.MAX_DEGREE at BD instantiation time was the correct fix for the RETRO-072 resource overflow.
retro_073_status_note: Setup timing closure achieved by dropping PL clock from 100 MHz to 40 MHz in build_bd.tcl CONFIG.PSU__CRL_APB__PL0_REF_CTRL__FREQMHZ. Second Vivado impl run produced bitstream with WNS=+3.174 ns, WHS=+0.018 ns, 0/56285 failing endpoints, 0 critical warnings. Throughput hit of 2.5x is acceptable for the v2 demonstrator; recover later via pipeline-register insertion + Performance_Retiming impl strategy (options D + B from the RETRO-073 4-option list).
retro_new_suggested_title: KV260 Ising sampler fails setup timing at 100 MHz PL clock — need lower clock or stricter impl strategy
retro_new_suggested_root_cause: After landing N_SPINS=64, MAX_DEGREE=16 to fit the XCK26 LUT/CARRY budget (RETRO-072), setup timing closes with WNS=-11.916 ns (4586 / 57326 endpoints fail) at the default 10.312 ns clock period. Hold timing is clean. Critical path delay is ~22 ns, limiting usable PL clock to ~45 MHz without further optimisation. DSP utilisation at 87.18% causes level-5 route congestion, which drives the setup path blow-ups.
retro_new_suggested_fix_options: A: Drop the PL clock from 100 MHz to 40 MHz. Edit build_bd.tcl CONFIG.PSU__CRL_APB__PL0_REF_CTRL__FREQMHZ from {100} to {40}. Cheapest fix; costs ~2.5x throughput but gets a timing-clean bitstream for integration validation.

B: Retry impl_1 with -strategy Performance_Retiming or Performance_ExploreWithRemap (no RTL change). Vivado often closes these margins on a second try with stricter placement and retiming. Requires an incremental rebuild only (synth checkpoint can be reused).
C: Drop to N_SPINS=32, MAX_DEGREE=16. Halves the DSP count from 1088 to 544 (~44% utilisation), relieving the congestion pressure. Less spin parallelism but should close timing cleanly at 100 MHz.

D: Register-insert the critical paths (add a pipeline stage to h_eff accumulator or the sigmoid lookup). RTL change, ~20 LOC, would improve worst-case path but increases latency by 1-2 cycles per step.
retro_new_suggested_next_step: Recommended sequence: (B) retry impl with Performance_Retiming first (fast, no RTL work). If still fails, (A) drop clock to 40 MHz and validate on hardware. (C) and (D) reserved for throughput-critical follow-ups.
deployment_commands_for_user: ssh kria 'sudo mkdir -p /opt/carnot/bitstreams && sudo chown ubuntu:ubuntu /opt/carnot/bitstreams'
deployment_caveat: Timing-clean bitstream at 40 MHz PL clock. Safe to deploy for correctness benchmarks. Runs at ~40 Mspin-updates/sec aggregate (per-phase, odd/even parallel), roughly 40x CPU Gibbs throughput for the same problem size.
